claim.why_it_matters: The whole figure is reduced to a bare, out-of-order list of node labels: no boxes, no decision shapes, no arrows, no branch targets. Every label token survives (3 'yes', 3 'no') but the connectivity — which is the entire content of the figure — is gone, and the residual reading order is scrambled (the three 'yes' labels are collected together after the last decision). The figure is unusable as a description of how 'condition-1 OR condition-2 AND condition-3' is evaluated. Adjacent pages 1176, 1177, 1185 and 1186 all received a proper ASCII-art rendering, so this is a pipeline drop, not a stylistic choice.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. Rendered p.1178 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v1178/spec_p1178.png, printed folio 1148) and read the markdown block at specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 47544-47588.

(1) The markdown quote is verbatim-accurate. Lines 47549-47583 are exactly the 14 label lines quoted, with nothing else between the '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' running head (line 47547) and the '**Figure D.10 ...**' caption (line 47585). There is no fenced ASCII-art block, no figure-notes prose block, and no adjacent-line reflow that could be carrying the lost structure. This is not page-break furniture, wrapping, or hyphenation — the entire graph is absent.

(2) The PDF quote is accurate. The render shows a complete flowchart: three rectangular process boxes (Evaluate condition-1 / -2 / -3), three rounded decision nodes (Condition-1 true, Condition-2 false, Condition-3 false), six labelled edges, a right-hand vertical channel and a left-hand vertical channel, and two arrowheaded terminals. I traced every edge: Condition-1 true yes -> right channel; no -> Evaluate condition-2. Condition-2 false yes -> LEFT channel; no -> Evaluate condition-3. Condition-3 false yes -> LEFT channel; no -> RIGHT channel. Left terminal reads 'Truth value is false', right terminal 'Truth value is true', with 'false' and 'true' underlined. That is exactly what the claim asserted.

(3) The claim's contested parenthetical about caption placement is CORRECT, and I verified it independently rather than taking it on faith. I rendered pp.1176, 1177 and 1179 as well. p.1176 prints the D.23 heading, then the caption 'Figure D.7 — Evaluation of the condition-1 AND condition-2 AND ... condition-n' ABOVE its diagram (an AND chain: Condition-n false yes -> 'Truth value is false', all-no -> 'Truth value is true'), then the 'Figure D.8' caption at the page foot. p.1177 carries the D.8 diagram (an OR chain over Condition-1/-2/-n true) with the 'Figure D.9' caption at its foot. p.1179 carries a four-condition diagram whose logic is exactly (c1 OR NOT c2) AND c3 AND c4 — i.e. Figure D.10's subject — and carries NO caption at all. The run is therefore caption-above-diagram throughout D.7-D.10, and the p.1178 diagram's logic (c1 true -> TRUE; else c2 false -> FALSE; else c3 false -> FALSE; else TRUE, i.e. c1 OR (c2 AND c3)) matches the D.9 caption text printed at the foot of p.1177. The claim identified the figure correctly.

(4) The 'pipeline drop, not stylistic choice' argument holds. pp.1176 and 1177 both carry fenced box-drawing ASCII art in the markdown (lines 47451-47487 and 47502-47536), and p.1186 does too (lines 47918-47956). So the transcription demonstrably can render these flowcharts and simply failed to here.

The loss is total and meaning-destroying: the figure's entire content IS its connectivity, and a reader of specs/ISO_COBOL.md at p.1178 gets an unordered bag of strings from which the evaluation order of 'condition-1 OR condition-2 AND condition-3' cannot be recovered. real=true.
verdict.corrected_description:
CONFIRMED as a structural figure loss, with four refinements to the reported description.

(a) The claim's figure identification and caption-placement analysis are correct and independently verified against renders of pp.1176/1177/1179: in the D.7-D.10 run the caption is printed ABOVE its diagram, so the p.1178 flowchart is Figure D.9 (Evaluation of condition-1 OR condition-2 AND condition-3) and the 'Figure D.10' caption at the foot of p.1178 heads the p.1179 diagram. The markdown reproduces the captions in the same above-the-diagram position, so the caption itself is not misplaced by the transcription — only the diagram is lost.

(b) The residual ordering is mis-described in one detail. The three 'yes' labels are NOT collected together after the last decision. The markdown order is: ... Condition-3 / false / yes / 'Truth value is false' / yes / yes / no / 'Truth value is true'. One 'yes' immediately follows the last decision, then the left-hand terminal intervenes, then the remaining two 'yes' and the third 'no' follow. The order is scrambled, just not in the shape stated. Token counts (3 'yes', 3 'no') are correct.

(c) An additional loss the claim did not mention: the underlining of 'false' and 'true' in the two terminals is dropped — the markdown renders bare 'is false' / 'is true'. In the printed standard the underline is the emphasis that marks the resulting truth value.

(d) The supporting comparison overstates p.1185 slightly and understates the defect's scope. pp.1176, 1177 and 1186 carry genuine fenced box-drawing ASCII art; p.1185's Figure D.11 got only an unfenced plain-text arrow sketch (still connectivity-preserving, but not box art). More importantly this is not an isolated page: p.1179 has the IDENTICAL defect — Figure D.10's four-condition flowchart is likewise reduced to a bare label list (specs/ISO_COBOL.md from line 47590). Any fix must cover pp.1178 and 1179 together. Separately, and outside this claim's scope, the p.1177 markdown's 'Figure notes' block (line 47538) annotates the p.1177 ASCII art as 'Figure D.9' when — by the caption-above-diagram convention just established — that diagram is Figure D.8's; that mislabel should be corrected in the same sweep.
